title: Microsoft Teams: Facilitator creates PowerPoint presentations from meeting discussions
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, licensing, preview qualifications and control paths are supported. Narrow the assurance that Facilitator never acts autonomously to the documented ability to request a deck, and correct the minor governance and citation gaps.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Users can ask Facilitator to create a PowerPoint presentation from meeting speech, chats and shared files.
claims.quote: you can ask Facilitator to create a PowerPoint presentation from what was said, chats, and shared files in the meeting.

claims.claim: Facilitator can already draft Word documents from meeting discussions.
claims.quote: Facilitator can already draft documents in Word, so now your team can also go straight from discussion to a deck.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Everyone in the meeting can see a user's prompts to Facilitator.
claims.quote: If a user prompts Facilitator, all users can view that communication, just like if the user was talking with another person in the meeting chat.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Facilitator posts its response in the meeting conversation for everyone to see, including unlicensed participants.
claims.quote: Facilitator then displays its response within the meeting's conversation for everyone to see.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated where generated deck files are saved or whose storage holds them.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Facilitator" "PowerPoint" "saved"' and '"Facilitator" "PowerPoint" "OneDrive"'; opened learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/facilitator-teams and purview/ai-teams-facilitator. Storage text describes .loop data, not generated decks.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the default sharing of generated decks.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Facilitator" "PowerPoint" permissions sharing sensitivity DLP' and '"Facilitator" "PowerPoint" "saved"'; opened learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/facilitator-teams. Meeting-response visibility is stated, but deck-file sharing is not.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Prevent copy and paste is not applied to Facilitator responses or AI-generated notes.
claims.quote: Meeting settings like Prevent copy and paste and Watermarks aren't applied to Facilitator's responses or AI-generated notes in meetings.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Watermarks are not applied to Facilitator responses or AI-generated notes.
claims.quote: Meeting settings like Prevent copy and paste and Watermarks aren't applied to Facilitator's responses or AI-generated notes in meetings.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Purview lists sensitivity labels as unsupported for Facilitator AI interactions.
claims.quote:
| Capability or solution in Microsoft Purview | Supported for AI interactions |
| Sensitivity labels | **✕** |

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Purview lists DLP as unsupported for Facilitator AI interactions.
claims.quote:
| Capability or solution in Microsoft Purview | Supported for AI interactions |

claims.claim: Facilitator AI-generated notes do not inherit the meeting's sensitivity label.
claims.quote: AI-generated notes for meetings don't inherit the meeting's sensitivity label; however, a sensitivity label can be applied to the notes' Loop component in the Loop app or OneDrive.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Meeting-label inheritance by generated decks is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Facilitator" "PowerPoint" permissions sharing sensitivity DLP'; opened facilitator-teams and ai-teams-facilitator; read sensitivity-labels-sharepoint-onedrive-files excerpts. General file labelling does not establish meeting-label inheritance for these decks.

claims.claim: No DLP rule is documented as preventing sensitive meeting content from being used to generate a Facilitator deck.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Facilitator" "PowerPoint" permissions sharing sensitivity DLP'; opened purview/ai-teams-facilitator and read dlp-sensitivity-label-as-condition excerpts. File DLP is documented, but no Facilitator deck-generation exclusion rule was found.

claims.claim: Only licensed users can initiate or prompt Facilitator.
claims.quote:
Only licensed userscan initiate Facilitator.
Unlicensed users can't prompt Facilitator, but they can see others' prompts to Facilitator and Facilitator's responses.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whose permissions are used to read shared files for deck creation.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Facilitator" "PowerPoint" "permissions"'; opened learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/facilitator-teams and purview/ai-teams-facilitator. Neither specifies the identity used to read shared files for deck creation.

claims.claim: Facilitator creates decks only when asked and does not act on its own.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Facilitator" "PowerPoint" autonomous automatically prompt'; opened facilitator-teams. The roadmap says users can ask for decks and Learn gives a prompt example; neither states the absolute exclusion of other initiation mechanisms.
claims.fix: Replace 'Facilitator creates the deck only when a user asks for it. It does not act on its own, but one participant’s request produces a file from everyone’s contributions.' with 'A user can ask Facilitator to create a deck from meeting discussions, chats and shared files.'

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Facilitator is included with a Microsoft Copilot licence, subject to available capacity, so existing Facilitator licensees need no new entitlement for this skill.
claims.quote: Facilitator is included with a Microsoft Copilot license and subject to available capacity. The following list contains the prerequisites for users to be able to access Facilitator features in Teams meetings.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope
claims.claim: Users need an eligible Microsoft 365 base licence.
claims.quote: An eligible Microsoft 365base license.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope
claims.claim: Users need an eligible Teams licence.
claims.quote: Have an eligible Microsoft Teamslicense.

claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot is available with Microsoft 365 E7 or as an add-on for eligible plans.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot is available with Microsoft 365 E7 or as an add-on for eligible commercial, US Government, and education subscription plans.

claims.claim: No meter specific to Facilitator deck creation is published.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Facilitator PowerPoint deck creation pricing meter capacity license'; opened facilitator-teams and copilot/plan/copilot-license-options. The feature is included subject to capacity; no deck-specific meter was found.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No separate price for Facilitator deck creation is published.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Facilitator PowerPoint deck creation pricing meter capacity license'; opened facilitator-teams and copilot/plan/copilot-license-options. Neither publishes a separate deck-creation price.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether generated decks count against a user's OneDrive storage.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Facilitator" "PowerPoint" "OneDrive"'; opened facilitator-teams; read OneDrive API overview excerpts. The deck's storage location and attribution to a user's quota are not specified.

claims.claim: Preview experiences require Microsoft Teams Public preview participation.
claims.quote: To use preview experiences, be a Microsoft Teams Public preview participant.

claims.claim: Facilitator is not supported in 1:1 chats, group chats, or external chats and meetings.
claims.quote: Currently, Facilitator isn't supported in 1:1 chats, group chats, or external chats and meetings.

claims.claim: Loop experiences in Teams must be enabled to use Facilitator in meetings.
claims.quote: Loop experiences in Teams need to be turned on in order for Facilitator to be used in meetings.

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Teams apps > Built-in Teams agents > agent > Edit availability controls who can use Facilitator.
claims.quote:
Sign in to the Teams admin center and go to Teams apps > Built-in Teams agents.
To change who can use an agent, select one or more agents and choose Edit availability.

claims.claim: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app id> -AppAssignmentType UsersAndGroups sets app availability, using -OperationType and -Users or -Groups for assignments.
claims.quote: This cmdlet allows administrators to modify app state, availability and installation status by adding or removing users and groups or changing assignment type or installation status.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/app-centric-management to sources. It links Update-M365TeamsApp for app availability and describes app-centric access for apps and Copilot agents; the Facilitator setup page expressly directs admins to app-centric management.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table and notes
claims.claim: The Facilitator setup page documents Teams apps > Manage apps > Facilitator > Allow or Block.
claims.quote:
In the left rail navigation, select Teams apps > Manage apps.
Select Facilitator from the app list.
In the actions menu, select Allow or Block.

claims.claim: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app id> -IsBlocked $true is a documented operation for changing tenant app state.
claims.quote:
PS C:\> Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -IsBlocked $true
-IsBlocked
The state of the app in the tenant.

claims.where: controls[2]; summary; What's changing; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: A separate admin UI or API switch for Facilitator PowerPoint deck creation is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Facilitator PowerPoint deck creation disable setting PowerShell Teams admin policy'; opened facilitator-teams, manage-apps and Update-M365TeamsApp. The skill-control section covers notes; no deck-only UI or command was found.

claims.claim: The setup page documents IsCollabMeetingNotesFluidEnabled for controlling AI-generated meeting notes.
claims.quote:
Loop experiences in Teams control AI-generated notes for meetings, which are enabled by default.
You can manage this control using the IsCollabMeetingNotesFluidEnabled setting in PowerShell.

claims.claim: The documented notes setting is tenant-wide rather than per-user.
claims.quote: This setting applies to your entire tenant and can't be configured at the user level.

claims.claim: Controlling availability of Facilitator as an agent governs access to all its skills, not only deck creation.
claims.quote: As an admin, you control whether Facilitator is available to your entire organization or to a certain group of users.

claims.claim: The setup page says blocking all apps for the organisation also blocks Facilitator.
claims.quote: However, if all apps are blocked for your organization, Facilitator is also blocked.

claims.claim: Retention of Facilitator AI interactions in meetings uses the Teams chats option.
claims.quote: For Facilitator AI interactions in meetings, use a retention policy with the Teams chats option.

claims.claim: Retention of Facilitator AI-generated meeting notes uses OneDrive accounts.
claims.quote: For Facilitator AI-generated notes in meetings, use a retention policy or retention labels with the OneDrive accounts option.

claims.claim: The Purview Facilitator page does not name deck files in its retention guidance.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Facilitator" "deck" audit retention'; opened learn.microsoft.com/purview/ai-teams-facilitator. Its retention instructions name Teams chats for interactions and OneDrive accounts for notes, not deck files.

claims.claim: The Update-M365TeamsApp reference describes Teams apps without specifically mentioning built-in agents.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Update-M365TeamsApp built-in Teams agents Facilitator availability block PowerShell'; opened learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams/update-m365teamsapp and checked its full text for built-in agents and Facilitator; neither is named.

claims.claim: Facilitator activity can be reviewed using Microsoft Purview Audit and DSPM for AI.
claims.quote: These events flow into activity explorer in the AI activities tab in the current version of DSPM and in DSPM for AI

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The checklist directs readers to review Purview Audit and DSPM for AI, but the controls table has no monitoring row.
claims.quote: Review Facilitator activity in Microsoft Purview Audit and DSPM for AI, and check whether deck creation appears there. The table contains only agent availability, app blocking and the separate deck-switch gap.
claims.fix: The After rollout step 'Review Facilitator activity in Microsoft Purview Audit and DSPM for AI, and check whether deck creation appears there' has no corresponding controls-table row. Remove this checklist step; do not add a row as part of this correction.

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Teams apps > Built-in Teams agents > Edit availability reaches the availability control.
claims.quote: To change who can use an agent, select one or more agents and choose Edit availability.
claims.fix: Replace the checklist path with 'Teams admin center > Teams apps > Built-in Teams agents > agent > Edit availability', matching controls[0].ui and making the agent-selection step explicit.

claims.claim: Purview's Facilitator page lists auditing support for notes, moderation and meeting Q&A, without identifying a deck-specific event.
claims.quote: Facilitator AI-generated notes, moderation, and questions and answers for meetings are supported.
